text: The file has data.users. Take users with active equal to true whose address.city equals "berlin" ignoring case (users with address null or without city do not match). Return an array of their name values sorted ascending alphabetically.
Each order has items with qty and price. For orders with status exactly "paid", sum qty*price over all their items. Return that total as a number rounded to 2 decimal places.
Ignore orders with status "cancelled". Count the remaining orders per customer. Return an object mapping customer to the number of orders.
Consider both dependencies and devDependencies together. Return the distinct package names whose version string starts with "^", as an array sorted ascending alphabetically.
For issues with state "open", count issues per assignee login. An issue whose assignee is null or missing is counted under the key "unassigned". Return an object mapping key to count.
Collect labels of issues with state "open", convert each label to lower case, and remove duplicates. Return an array sorted ascending alphabetically.

Each line is: timestamp, level, service, message... The second token is the level and the third token is the service. Count lines with level ERROR per service. Return an object mapping service to count (only services having at least one ERROR).
Lines end with a token took=<N>ms. For lines whose service (third token) is "api", at any level, compute the average of N. Return a number rounded to 1 decimal place.

CSV with a header row (name,dept,salary,start_date). Rows with an empty salary are ignored entirely. Compute the average salary per dept, rounded to the nearest integer. Return an object mapping dept to that integer (depts with no salaries are omitted).
CSV with a header row. Ignoring rows with an empty salary, sort by salary descending, ties broken by name ascending, and return the names of the first 3 as an array.

Plain key=value lines; lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored. Take keys that start with "db.", remove that "db." prefix, and return an object of the remaining key to its value; all values stay strings.
For events with type "click", read payload.user.id. Skip events where payload, user or id is null or missing. Return the number of distinct ids.

Consider products whose stock is a number greater than 0 (null stock does not count). For each build an object {"sku": sku, "value": price*stock rounded to 2 decimals}. Sort by value descending and return the first 3 objects as an array.

Given this comma-separated list of email addresses: "alice@Example.com, Bob@example.com, carol@test.org, ALICE@example.com, dave@test.org, erin@Test.org, bob@EXAMPLE.com, frank@demo.net". Trim spaces and compare case-insensitively, so addresses differing only in case are the same. Return an object mapping the lower-cased domain (part after @) to the number of distinct addresses with that domain.
